samples.summary: `parseMarginFromEdgeAttr('')` returns 0 where both previous readers returned the default
samples.evidence: Both readers previously used a truthiness guard: backend `docs-tree.ts` had `attrs.marginFromEdge ? Number(attrs.marginFromEdge) : DEFAULT_HEADER_MARGIN_FROM_EDGE` and the frontend store had `Number(attrs.marginFromEdge ?? '48')`. The new `parseMarginFromEdgeAttr` only guards on `value === undefined` and `Number.isFinite`, so an empty-string attribute (`Number('') === 0`, finite) now yields `marginFromEdge: 0` instead of 48 — the header/footer renders flush against the page edge rather than at the default inset. The sibling numeric-field parse in the same module has the same `Number('') === 0` behaviour, and the new backend spec even asserts it for `marginLeft: ''` (docs-tree.spec.ts, "`Number('')` is 0, not NaN"), showing the empty-attribute case is reachable in the codec's own model of legacy data.

samples.summary: New slides validators recurse without a depth bound, so a deeply nested payload throws RangeError (500) instead of returning 400
samples.evidence: `assertValidElement` recurses into `data.children` for `type === 'group'` (line 552-554) and `assertValidTextBodyBlocks` recurses into nested docs table cells (line 616), both with no depth limit. A PUT body with a few thousand nested groups (or nested docs tables in a slide text body) overflows the stack inside the validator itself, producing an unhandled RangeError → 500 from the very endpoint whose stated purpose in these comments is to convert malformed payloads into 400s. `assertValidBlock`'s nested-table recursion has the same shape and is now reachable from header/footer blocks too.

samples.summary: PPTX `colorChildXml` now substitutes opaque black for any color it cannot normalize, including fully-transparent ones
samples.evidence: `const hex = toRgbHexColor(c.value) ?? '000000';` — `toRgbHexColor` deliberately returns `undefined` for a fully transparent color (`rgba(...,0)` / `#RRGGBB00`, see color.ts:128 and :136). At this sink that maps to `000000`, so a shape fill / slide background / gradient stop that is invisible on screen exports as a solid black region covering slide content, rather than being dropped or preserved. The same fallback also converts any unrecognised-but-meaningful CSS form (e.g. `rgb(255 0 0)` space-separated, `red`) into black. Callers that could omit the color (text.ts) do drop it; the fill sinks cannot, so the failure mode lands here.

samples.summary: Issue-#728 empty-string guard was not applied to the border-color canvas sink
samples.evidence: `ctx.strokeStyle = border.color;` assigns a persisted `BorderStyle.color` straight to the context. This is the same failure mode the diff fixed for text/underline/list-marker fills: an empty (or otherwise invalid) color string is silently ignored by the canvas, leaving whatever the previous pass set (the selection/highlight stroke). `parseBorderStyle` in both stores builds `color` from a raw comma-split attribute with no validation (yorkie-doc-store.ts:283-287), so `color: ''` is representable. The sweep guarded every fill sink in paint-layout.ts and table-renderer.ts but left this stroke sink unguarded.

samples.summary: `applyBlockStyle` can now leave a stale CRDT attribute while the in-memory cache records the new value
samples.evidence: `const attrs = serializeBlockStyle(merged); ... tree.styleByPath(blockPath, attrs);` — `serializeBlockStyleAttrs` now OMITS any field whose value is non-finite/undefined (crdt-attrs.ts:67-72), and `styleByPath` only merges. Previously every field was written unconditionally, so the node always matched `merged`. Now if a caller supplies a non-finite value (e.g. a `Number(...)`/`parseFloat` result from a UI input reaching `applyBlockStyle({ lineHeight })` at docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:371), the cache is updated to `block.style = merged` while the Tree keeps the previous attribute — the local view and the persisted/reloaded document diverge silently instead of failing.

samples.summary: `toRgbHexColor` treats an empty alpha group as fully transparent and drops an opaque color
samples.evidence: The regex's alpha group is `(?:,([^)]*))?`, so `rgb(255,0,0,)` captures `''`; `isTransparentAlpha('')` computes `Number('') === 0`, which is finite and `<= 0`, so the function returns `undefined` and the caller drops a color whose RGB channels are perfectly usable. The comment on `isTransparentAlpha` states the opposite intent ("anything unparseable is treated as opaque").

samples.summary: `removeNodeStyle` relies on unverified `Tree.pathToIndex` / `Tree.removeStyle` index semantics on a hot path
samples.evidence: `const from = tree.pathToIndex(path); tree.removeStyle(from, from + 1, attrsToRemove);` replaces `removeStyleByPath` in three places, including `applyBlockType` (line 1459), which runs on nearly every block-type change because `toRemove` almost always contains `headingLevel`. If `pathToIndex` returns a position that is not the node's opening-tag index (or `removeStyle` has a different arity/name in the pinned SDK), the removal either silently no-ops (stale `headingLevel`/`listKind` attributes survive a block-type change) or throws inside `doc.update`. packages/frontend has no `tsc` lane, so nothing type-checks these calls; only the vitest suite would surface it.

finding.summary: PPTX `colorChildXml` now substitutes opaque black for any color it cannot normalize, including fully-transparent ones
finding.evidence: `const hex = toRgbHexColor(c.value) ?? '000000';` — `toRgbHexColor` deliberately returns `undefined` for a fully transparent color (`rgba(...,0)` / `#RRGGBB00`, see color.ts:128 and :136). At this sink that maps to `000000`, so a shape fill / slide background / gradient stop that is invisible on screen exports as a solid black region covering slide content, rather than being dropped or preserved. The same fallback also converts any unrecognised-but-meaningful CSS form (e.g. `rgb(255 0 0)` space-separated, `red`) into black. Callers that could omit the color (text.ts) do drop it; the fill sinks cannot, so the failure mode lands here.

verdict.reason: The quoted code exists verbatim: packages/slides/src/export/pptx/color.ts:59 substitutes '000000' whenever toRgbHexColor returns undefined. toRgbHexColor (packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:127-130, :136, :143, helper :82-86) deliberately returns undefined for fully transparent colors (#RRGGBB00, rgba(...,0)) and for any unrecognized CSS form (named colors, space-separated rgb()), as its own tests confirm (packages/docs/test/model/color.test.ts:255-257, :263). Unlike text.ts:208, which drops the attribute on undefined, the fill sinks must emit a color and therefore render black: shape.ts:96 and :144 only branch on the fill being absent, so a present-but-transparent fill yields <a:solidFill><a:srgbClr val="000000"/></a:solidFill> instead of <a:noFill/>; the same applies to slide background (slide.ts:89), master background (master.ts:31), table cell fill (table.ts:128) and gradient stops (color.ts:77). Reachability is real: migrate.ts:170-173 wraps arbitrary legacy string fills into {kind:'srgb', value} unfiltered, and the model accepts persisted values from import/content API (documented in color.ts:52-58). No upstream guard filters transparent or named-color fills, so the black-substitution path is live and produces an opaque region covering slide content — a wrong-output correctness bug in this lens's lane. No named refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: Frontend header/footer `marginFromEdge` read was left without the NaN guard the backend copy just got — a legacy/poisoned attribute still yields NaN in the renderer
finding.evidence: The change hardens the backend reader (`parseMarginFromEdge` in packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:353 falls back to DEFAULT_HEADER_MARGIN_FROM_EDGE for any non-finite attribute) and adds a backend test for the literal string `"undefined"`. The frontend store — the code that actually lays out and paints the header — still does `marginFromEdge: Number(attrs.marginFromEdge ?? '48')` at lines 526 and 532, so a node written by the pre-guard serializer (`marginFromEdge: "undefined"`) reads back as `NaN`. That NaN flows into `getHeaderYStart`/`getFooterYStart` (packages/docs/src/view/pagination.ts:260,274) and `doc-canvas.ts:272/318`, i.e. NaN geometry in the layout/paint path — exactly the failure mode the backend fix declares unacceptable. The companion writer at lines 728/769/2724/2732 also still does `String(header.marginFromEdge)`, so an absent value is re-persisted as the literal "undefined" instead of being omitted like `serializeMarginFromEdge` now does on the backend.

verdict.reason: The described code does not exist in the frontend store. The finding claims `marginFromEdge: Number(attrs.marginFromEdge ?? '48')` at yorkie-doc-store.ts:526/532, but the header/footer reads are at :492 and :498 and both call `parseMarginFromEdge(attrs.marginFromEdge)`; lines 526-532 belong to `readPageSetup` and read paperSize/margins fields, never marginFromEdge. Frontend and backend share ONE codec rather than having divergent copies: the frontend imports `serializeMarginFromEdgeAttrs`/`parseMarginFromEdgeAttr` from @wafflebase/docs (:42-43, aliased :221-222), exactly as the backend does (docs-tree.ts:30,32,270,294). `parseMarginFromEdgeAttr` (packages/docs/src/model/crdt-attrs.ts:121-125) returns DEFAULT_HEADER_MARGIN_FROM_EDGE for undefined and for any non-finite parse, so the literal "undefined" attribute reads back as the default in the frontend too — no NaN can reach getHeaderYStart/getFooterYStart. The writer claim is likewise false: the four frontend write sites (:694, :735, :2689, :2697) all call `serializeMarginFromEdge(...)`, which returns {} for undefined/null and {} for non-finite (crdt-attrs.ts:107-113), omitting the field rather than writing "undefined". A repo-wide grep for the quoted patterns yields zero source hits; the only matches are stale snippets in an archived planning doc (docs/tasks/archive/2026/04/20260408-header-footer-todo.md:1155,1160), which appears to be what the reviewer actually quoted.

finding.summary: New `style.alignment` whitelist on PUT disagrees with the reader, which passes any string through — a read-modify-write (CLI pull/push) of a document holding a legacy alignment value now 400s
finding.evidence: `assertValidBlockStyle` rejects any `style.alignment` not in {left,center,right,justify}. But `parseBlockStyle` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:177 and the frontend copy at yorkie-doc-store.ts:244) accepts *any* string, including the literal "undefined" that the old unconditional serializer (`alignment: style.alignment` with an undefined value) could have persisted, and any other legacy token. So GET returns `style.alignment: "undefined"` and the very next PUT of that untouched body is rejected with 400 — the round-trip the controller comment calls "identity on the JSON shape" is no longer identity for such documents. The numeric fields were deliberately hardened on the read side (non-finite → default) but `alignment` was not, leaving validator and reader inconsistent.

finding.summary: Block-style validation checks alignment values but still lets `style: {}` through, persisting the literal string "undefined" and NaN geometry into the CRDT
finding.evidence: The new test explicitly asserts `{ blocks: [{ id, type:'paragraph', style: {}, inlines: [] }] }` passes validation. `writeDocsRoot`'s `serializeBlockStyle` then produces `alignment: undefined` and `lineHeight: String(undefined) === 'undefined'` (docs-tree.ts:143-148); `parseBlockStyle` (line 159) does `Number('undefined') → NaN` and `normalizeBlockStyle` spreads that NaN over the default, so `marginTop`/`lineHeight` become NaN and `computeLayout`'s `y += block.style.marginTop` NaNs out the whole document layout. If the controller is now validating block-style *values*, the required numeric fields are the ones that actually corrupt the document when missing.

verdict.reason: The claimed corruption path does not exist in this repository. `docs-tree.ts:145-146` aliases `serializeBlockStyle`/`parseBlockStyle` to the shared codec in `@wafflebase/docs` (imported at lines 28-33), not a local `String(undefined)` implementation — the cited "docs-tree.ts:143-148" is a comment. The codec guards exactly the fields named: `serializeBlockStyleAttrs` (crdt-attrs.ts:62-74) omits absent alignment via `isBlockAlignment` and skips `undefined`/`null`/non-finite numerics (`if (raw === undefined || raw === null) continue;` + `if (Number.isFinite(value))`), so no literal `"undefined"` is ever persisted; `parseBlockStyleAttrs` (crdt-attrs.ts:86-98) only copies finite numerics and known alignments into the partial before `normalizeBlockStyle`, so even a legacy stored `"undefined"` → NaN is dropped instead of spread over `DEFAULT_BLOCK_STYLE` (types.ts:216-223, 272-274). Both behaviors are regression-tested with the exact `style: {}` payload from the finding: docs-tree.spec.ts:102-137 asserts alignment defaults to 'left', all numerics finite, no 'undefined' in the serialized style, and that `lineHeight`/`alignment` attributes are absent from the CRDT; docs-tree.spec.ts:139-157 covers the legacy poisoned-attribute read.
